tropes.html:
The portrayal of Fat Bastard's participation in professional Sumo is strictly for laughs, as described in this video by retired Sumo champion Konishiki Yasokichi; specific errors include:
  • Fat Bastard is wearing shoes and socks, while Sumo requires participants to be barefoot.
  • His victory by Groin Attack would be completely illegal; moreover, the mawashi (loincloth) is far too tough to pinch through.

tropes.name: As Long as It Sounds Foreign
tropes.html: Fook Yu, Fook Mi, and Mr. Roboto are not authentic Japanese names.

tropes.name: Big Bad Duumvirate
tropes.html: Dr. Evil teams up with Goldmember against Austin Powers.

tropes.name: Bitch Slap
tropes.html: Upon reuniting with Foxxy Cleopatra, Foxxy uses a random disco man (played by Nathan Lane) as a cover to talk to Austin. In the middle of their conversation, Foxxy/Disco Man slaps Austin out of the blue, calling out Austin for not contacting her for 8 years.

tropes.name: Blaxploitation
tropes.html: While the franchise is mainly a parody of the Bond films, Foxxy Cleopatra is clearly a Genre Refugee from films like Shaft and Super Fly.

tropes.name: Bowdlerize
tropes.html: In-universe, this was the case for Dr. Evil's "It's a Hard Knock Life" music video: Nudity was censored, and Dr. Evil's curse words were edited, radio edit-style.

tropes.name: Bread, Eggs, Milk, Squick
tropes.html:
Austin's "Things to Do Before I Die" checklist:
Become International Man of Mystery.
Save World From Certain Doom.
Find True Love.
Go To Outer Space.
Travel Through Time, Backward and Forward.
Be Cryogenically Frozen.
Catch Dr. Evil in the First Act.
Threesome with Japanese Twins.
Earn Daddy's Respect.

tropes.name: Breaking Old Trends
tropes.html:
Several elements shown in the previous two movies are absent here.
  • There are no Laugh-In-inspired scene transitions.
  • This movie lacks a scene where one of Dr. Evil's Mooks is killed, and Austin launches into a Hurricane of Puns revolving around the circumstances of the death.
  • Austin's Union Jack briefs don't appear.

tropes.name: Breast Attack
tropes.html: Austin subjects Fat Bastard to a double purple nurple during their brief fight.

tropes.name: Bucket List
tropes.html: Austin has one that pulls out to cross off "Threesome with Japanese twins", after the two twins propose one with him. However, since this movie predates the trope naming film by four years, it's here referred to by the decidedly more on the nose "Things to Do Before I Die" instead.

tropes.name: Cameo Cluster
tropes.html: The opening is full of famous people playing themselves on the set of an In-Universe Austin Powers movie, which is being directed by Steven Spielberg and stars Tom Cruise, Gwyneth Paltrow, Kevin Spacey, and Danny DeVito, with Quincy Jones ("This is where the movie gets its mojo, baby.") and Britney Spears (or a fembot thereof) doing the music.

tropes.name: Captain Obvious
tropes.html: Goldmember states the obvious when Dr. Evil starts giving Scott preferential treatment: "It's a power struggle." and "The tiny one can't take the hint."

tropes.name: Casting Gag
tropes.html: Harry Palmer himself, Michael Caine, appears as Nigel Powers.

tropes.name: Circle of Shame
tropes.html: This happens twice to Austin as the crowd reacts to his father not being there at a royal award and, in flashback, winning an award at spy academy - and there's a toothless old gardener laughing at him both times. To add even more injury, it's the SAME toothless gardener!

tropes.name: Compressed Hair
tropes.html: After swimming to Dr. Evil's submarine Foxxy removes her swimcap to reveal short-looking hair. She shakes her head and it explodes, via a cut to Austin, into her usual enormous afro.

tropes.name: Consulting a Convicted Killer
tropes.html: After Austin learns that his father, Nigel, has been kidnapped and the only clue is that the crew of his yacht have had their genitalia painted gold, Austin visits Dr. Evil, who is being held in captivity in a cell much like Hannibal Lecter's, to find out who is responsible. Dr. Evil reveals to Austin that Goldmember is behind the abduction.

tropes.name: Continuity Nod
tropes.html: At the end of the first movie, Basil tells Austin that he will be knighted. Early on in this film, Austin is finally knighted.

tropes.name: Conveyor Belt o' Doom
tropes.html:
Parodies a very similar scene from Goldfinger with Austin's dad strapped to a device that moves him genitals-first towards a container pouring molten gold.
Goldmember: Your fajah is about to have an unfortunate smelting accident!

tropes.name: Daddy Didn't Show
tropes.html: Nigel Powers had a tendency for this, to the point Austin starts singing "Daddy Wasn't There", quoted atop that article.

tropes.name: Daddy Issues
tropes.html:
Austin responds to accusations of having "Daddy Issues" with this:
Austin: "Nothing could be My Father from the truth. For me this is a Dad issue....Dead! Dad! Deadbeat dad! Daddy didn't love me!"

tropes.name: Dark Horse Victory
tropes.html: As shown in a Flashback, Dr. Evil was actually the favorite to win the prestigious "International Man of Mystery" position at the secret agent academy. But despite this, Austin ended up receiving that honor instead.

tropes.name: Dead Partner
tropes.html: Foxxy Cleopatra had a partner who was killed by Goldmember, and is determined to bring the villain to justice for it.

tropes.name: Denser and Wackier
tropes.html: Goldmember relies less on parodies of the spy genre and more on broad humor, celebrity cameos and pop culture references that were trending in 2002.

tropes.name: Didn't We Use This Joke Already?
tropes.html:
When they reuse the rocket-joke from the second movie.
Ozzy: These filmmakers are just [bleep] boobs!
Kelly: What do you mean, Dad?
Ozzy: Well, they're usin' the same [bleep] jokes they did in the last Austin Powers movie.

tropes.name: DreamWorks Face
tropes.html: The Dr. Evil giant submarine has one. Of course it's based on Dr. Evil's quirk of doing the same thing.

tropes.name: Dude, Not Funny!
tropes.html: Said In-Universe by Austin in regards to his father writing off Austin's quite legitimate complaints about his parenting skills with a joke.

tropes.name: Dull Surprise
tropes.html: The street-market shopper (Fred Stoller) who appears in the third section of the montage ("Are they nice and firm?") has this reaction to the satellite's coming into view.

tropes.name: EgoCorp
tropes.html: Dr Evil has a business arrangement with Mr Roboto, a Japanese businessman and owner of Roboto Industries.

tropes.name: Even the Subtitler Is Stumped
tropes.html: When Austin reunites with his father, in order to prevent the two American women who were keeping tabs on them from knowing what they are talking about, they opt to discus the details in English English, and communicate entirely in increasingly more nonsensical Cockney slang. The subtitler eventually gives up.

tropes.name: Everyone Went to School Together
tropes.html: It is revealed that Austin, Dr. Evil, Number Two and Basil all went to the secret agent academy at the same time (with Austin and Dr. Evil even sharing a dormitory).

tropes.name: Evil Diva
tropes.html: Britney Spears in the opening sequence, whom confidently rivals Austin in a dance battle, and reveals herself to be a Fembot assassin.

tropes.name: Expository Hairstyle Change
tropes.html: Not actually plot-driven, but Foxxy Cleopatra's hairstyle changes in virtually every new scene she's in.

tropes.name: Faceship
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's sub is modeled after him.

tropes.name: Fake Film Intro
tropes.html: The film opens with an action scene where the series' main characters have now been suspiciously recast - Austin Powers is portrayed by Tom Cruise, Dr. Evil by Kevin Spacey and Mini Me by Danny DeVito. It then cuts to a sound stage, revealing that the opening is just part of an in-universe Austin Powers movie being directed by Steven Spielberg.

tropes.name: Fake-Out Opening
tropes.html: The movie opens with a scene from a film within the film about Austin's life.

tropes.name: Flanderization
tropes.html:
Especially evident in Austinpussy (the movie-within-a-movie in Goldmember).
John Travolta as Goldmember: Hey, assholes! Do I have time for a last smoke and a pancake or what!?

tropes.name: Flashback Cut
tropes.html:
• There's a brief cut back to Dr. Evil's "Not So Different" Remark from the first movie.
  • Austin has one when Mini-Me flashes the "peace" symbol. He did this only to give him the finger and kick Austin in the face.

tropes.name: Freeze-Frame Bonus
tropes.html: The email Austin gets reads "Dear Customer: You are being sent a new credit card by FedEx because your old one was hacked while you were browsing iPods on eBay. Sincerely, Your Bank."

tropes.name: Freudian Slip
tropes.html:
• Austin repeatedly saying "dad" or "father" instead of other words.
Dr. Evil: Uh oh! Somebody's got some daddy issues!
Austin: Nothing could be my father from the truth.
Dr. Evil: Oop... you said "my father."
Austin: No I dadn't!
Dr. Evil: HOW!
Austin: Didn't! Did not!
Dr. Evil: Shappah!
Austin: For me, this is a dad issue.
Dr. Evil: Oop.
Austin: Dead issue! Dead... dead dad! Deadbeat dad! Daddy didn't love me!
  • Austin suffers from a similiar situation with Number Three.
Austin: Nice to mole you-meet you! Nice to meet your mole. ...Moley, moley, moley, moley!

tropes.name: Fun with Subtitles
tropes.html:
Mr. Roboto, when talking to Austin Powers and Foxxy Cleopatra, speaks in subtitles. With the series's usual No Fourth Wall comedy, the white objects in Mr. Roboto's room obscure some of his subtitles which are mistaken for much dirtier phrases until they are clarified. This is promptly Lampshaded by Austin Powers after Mr. Roboto reveals he can speak English the entire time.
Austin: Yeah, why don't you? That way I wouldn't misread the subtitles making it seem like you are saying things which are dirty. [looks to camera]

tropes.name: Great Escape
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's escape from normal prison involves starting a Prison Riot to cover the escape. He was able to manipulate the prison's populace after demonstrating how, you know, evil he is.

tropes.name: Gross-Up Close-Up
tropes.html: Whenever Number Three appears, there is always a zoom-in on his gigantic mole. He even twitches it a little...

tropes.name: Hair Reboot
tropes.html: Foxxy Cleopatra's hair goes from a fairly flat style from being wet to her full-out Funny Afro after she shakes her head.

tropes.name: Help Mistaken for Attack
tropes.html: Austin returns to his hotel room to find Mini-Me grinning at him while holding up a letter opener. The audience knows that Mini-Me is here because he defected from Dr. Evil (the "help") and that he was just using the letter opener to open some mail, but Austin immediately reads it as an ambush (the "attack") and gives him a sound thrashing.

tropes.name: Hoist by His Own Petard
tropes.html: Mini-Me's I Surrender, Suckers! on the Moon Base in the previous film comes back to bite him in the ass during his defection. Austin (who doesn't realize Mini-Me is defecting) thinks this an assassination attempt and attacks the clone. When Mini-Me tries to deescalate things, Austin thinks he's just pulling the same crap he did on the Moon Base and refuses to fall for it again. Mini-Me, with a pained look on his face, is all too aware of the trope.

tropes.name: Hurricane of Euphemisms
tropes.html:
In a Call-Back to a popular gag from the previous film, Dr. Evil causes a satellite to fall out of orbit, and it happens to resemble a pair of—
Beautiful Fruit Vendor: Melons! [holds up two melons in front of her rack] Big juicy melons!
Customer: [suggestively] Are they nice and firm?
Beautiful Fruit Vendor: [seductively] Well, what do you think?
Customer: Look at that! It looks like a set of giant—
[Cut to a sporting event where four shirtless fans have the word "TITS" painted on their stomachs.]
Second T: Hey, "A" and "N", you're late!
N: How're we doin'? Yeah!
Fans: Let's go, Titans!
A: Check it out, those remind me of—
Ozzy Osbourne: Boobs!
Sharon Osbourne: "Boobs", Ozzy?
Ozzy: These filmmakers are just [bleep]ing boobs.
Kelly Osbourne: What do you mean, Dad?
Ozzy: Well, they're using the same [bleep]ing joke as they did in the last Austin Powers movie.
Sharon: What [bleep]ing joke?
Jack Osbourne: Y'know, the [bleep]ing joke about the long smooth rocket that looks like some guy's—
Colonel: Johnson!
Johnson: Yes, sir?
Colonel: Any sign of that satellite?
Johnson: No, sir, it's gone.

tropes.name: Hypocritical Humor
tropes.html: There's two things Nigel Powers can't stand: "people who are intolerant of other people's cultures...and the Dutch!"

tropes.name: Ignore the Disability
tropes.html:
Number Three's mole. Around it, everyone feels inclined to unintentionally make stupid puns. "Why, thank yo— MOLE!!!" "Moley, moley, moley, moley, moley!"
  • Later defied when Number Three tells Austin to just get it out of his system. Austin gladly obliges.

tropes.name: I Resemble That Remark!
tropes.html: After Ozzy Osbourne complains that the filmmakers are just using the same [bleep]ing joke as they did in the last Austin Powers movie, the Hurricane of Euphemisms proceeds to end again with the pun "Johnson!" yelled by a colonel, even involving the exact same two actors for it.

tropes.name: Irony
tropes.html: Number Three lampshades this, noting that he is a mole who happens to have a rather large mole on his face.

tropes.name: Knighting
tropes.html: Austin gets knighted after catching Dr. Evil. Goes from being a cool moment to a sad one when his father doesn't show up.

tropes.name: Lame Pun Reaction
tropes.html: Dr. Evil: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to my submarine lair. It's long, hard and full of seamen! [nobody laughs] Nothing? Not even a titter?

tropes.name: Lawyer-Friendly Cameo
tropes.html: While the group are pursuing Goldmember, Nigel's car crashes into a float that looks like Godzilla, but due to international copyright laws, isn't actually Godzilla.

tropes.name: Medium Awareness
tropes.html:
Austin uses the subtitles to understand Japanese. What makes it funny is that the white subtitles are sometimes placed in front of white items, resulting in the subtitles looking entirely lewd.
Mr. Roboto: Why don't I just, uh, speak in English?
Austin: Yes, that would be helpful! Then we wouldn't continue to misread your subtitles, making it seem that you're saying things that are dirty! [cracks smile just before camera cuts away]

tropes.name: Meeting-the-Parents Sequel
tropes.html: Austin's Father is introduced. Kind of odd that his dad is still alive, given how Austin is from the 60s, though the movie doesn't even bother to explain it.

tropes.name: Mook Chivalry
tropes.html: "Look, here's how it goes, you attack me one at a time and I knock you out with one punch, okay? Go."

tropes.name: Moonwalk Dance
tropes.html: Scott Evil performs a moonwalk just before the end credits.

tropes.name: Never the Selves Shall Meet
tropes.html: Austin and Dr. Evil travel back in time to feud in the seventies while their "past" selves during that era are still in cryogenic suspension.

tropes.name: Nominal Importance
tropes.html:
Nigel Powers talks one of Dr. Evil's minions out of attacking him by pointing this out.
Nigel Powers: Have you any idea how many anonymous henchmen I've killed? Look at you! You don't even have a name tag! You've got no chance. Why don't you just fall down?
[the henchman falls down]

tropes.name: Not Even Bothering with the Accent
tropes.html: Tom Cruise uses his British accent while playing Austin in the In-Universe movie based on Austin's adventures.

tropes.name: Notzilla
tropes.html:
Lampshaded with two Japanese men running from a monster statue that vaguely resembles Godzilla during the car chase in Japan:
Japanese Man 1: RUUUUN!!! IT'S GODZILLA!
Japanese Man 2: It looks like Gojira, but due to international copyright laws, it's not.
Japanese Man 1: STILL, WE SHOULD RUN LIKE IT IS GODZILLA!
Japanese Man 2: [glances at the camera] Though it isn't.

tropes.name: Overt Rendezvous
tropes.html: Austin and Foxxy Cleopatra meet on a public bench, but with a man (Nathan Lane) sitting in between them, who moves his lips without speaking while Foxxy is the one actually talking. This way, to any outsider, it looks like Austin and the man are the only ones having a conversation.

tropes.name: Parental Neglect
tropes.html: Nigel was absent for most of the major events in Austin's life, including his graduation from secret agent academy.

tropes.name: Pixellation
tropes.html: Used on a woman's bare breasts in the "Hard Knock Life" music video.

tropes.name: Precision F-Strike
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's response to being caught in the first act, before even getting started on his Evil Plan, is simply "... shit."

tropes.name: Pretty Fly for a White Guy
tropes.html: Dr. Evil and Mini-Me performing a music video to the tune of "It's A Hard Knock Life" is all about parodying this. From the high and squeaky singing voice to the abrupt costume change, it is mockery.

tropes.name: Random Events Plot
tropes.html: The first half of the film. There's no reason given why Dr. Evil wants Nigel Powers abducted (while there are several plausible, justifiable reasons, he's never shown an interest in Austin's father before), why Nigel was taken to Goldmember's club in 1975 instead of just held somewhere in the present, or how Dr. Evil arranged his abduction from prison.note The opening scene implied Dr. Evil hadn't made contact with Goldmember yet. While it is possible that Number 2 or someone else could have contacted Goldmember and planned the abduction afterward, Dr. Evil either wouldn't know or had such a back-up plan in place already, and that just raises more questions. It is also unclear why Dr. Evil would reveal this to Austin when he could have sent him on a wild goose chase to somewhere else. The trope could be considered justified given the franchise is primarily a comedy, and Dr. Evil isn't known for his well thought-out plans, but it's still quite disjointed compared to the first two films. Once the action moves to Japan, things settle down into a more coherent plot structure.

tropes.name: Red Right Hand
tropes.html:
Goldmember's calling card is covering his victims' genitals in gold paint.
Goldmember: Dr. Evil, can I paint his [Nigel Powers'] yoo-hoo gold? It's kind of my thing, you know.
Dr. Evil: (pilots his mechanical chair up close to Goldmember) How about "No", you crazy Dutch bastard?!

tropes.name: Rent-a-Zilla
tropes.html: In a film series that parodies mostly James Bond films, a Notzilla appears.

tropes.name: Request for Privacy
tropes.html: Parodied. When Dr. Evil's son starts becoming evil himself, Dr. Evil shouts how it's getting a little crowded in the submarine deck they're all in and orders everyone to leave. Everyone starts getting up, but Dr. Evil then starts saying "Not you" followed by various people. By the time he's saying who doesn't have to leave, only Mini-Me hasn't been ordered to stay, making it apparent who Dr. Evil wants out of the room.

tropes.name: Retroactive Idiot Ball
tropes.html: This movie establishes that Austin and Dr. Evil went to the spy academy together. This makes Dr. Evil's attempt to pull a Luke, I Am Your Father on Austin in the previous movie (and Austin actually considering it to be a possibility) make them both look rather foolish in hindsight.

tropes.name: Reverse Polarity
tropes.html: Trying to stop the MIDAS asteroid from crashing into Earth and flooding it.

tropes.name: Self-Deprecation
tropes.html: Ozzy Osbourne: Boobs! These writers are a bunch of boobs!

tropes.name: Separated by a Common Language
tropes.html: There's a scene where Nigel Powers is talking about his sexual exploits and Austin requests that they speak in "English" English in front of the Americans. The proceeding conversation has subtitles. (But not all of it.)

tropes.name: Show Within a Show
tropes.html: Austinpussy, originally the intended title of this installment (a parody of Octopussy), which they couldn't get past the censors. It was directed by Steven Spielberg and starred Tom Cruise as Austin, Gwyneth Paltrow as the Bond Girl, Kevin Spacey as Dr. Evil, Danny DeVito as Mini-Me, and John Travolta as Goldmember.

tropes.name: Sir Swears-a-Lot
tropes.html: In a parody of late '90s/early 00s rap, one of the verses in Dr. Evil's "Hard Knock Life" rap is nearly completely censored from the amount of swearing.

tropes.name: Sound-Effect Bleep
tropes.html: Utilized during the cutaway to the Osbournes.

tropes.name: Sparing the Final Mook
tropes.html: When taken before Dr. Evil and Goldmember, Nigel effortlessly knocks out two mooks, then notices a third and final mook, who is obviously scared of him. Nigel decides to take it easy on the third guy, telling him to just act like Nigel knocked him out too and nobody will hold it against him. The mook quickly goes along with it.

tropes.name: Stealth Pun
tropes.html: The movie-within-a-movie has Mini-Me firing off an M-249 machine gun, also known as the "Minimi".

tropes.name: Swapped Roles
tropes.html: In the previous movie, Dr. Evil showed blatant favoritism to Mini-Me over Scott. In this movie, Dr. Evil and Scott's relationship has greatly improved and Mini-Me finds himself being phased out of Dr. Evil's inner circle, resulting in him turning on the villainous doctor and siding with the good guys.

tropes.name: Sweet Tooth
tropes.html: Mini Me is shown to have a near-obsessive love of chocolate, Dr. Evil noting that the food is like "catnip for clones".

tropes.name: Taught by Experience
tropes.html: Played for dramatic irony with Austin when Mini-Me tries to defect (and Austin thinks the clone's trying to kill him again). When Mini-Me tries to peacefully surrender, Austin (who's been left out of the loop about the defection) doesn't believe him. After all, this is ''exactly'' what Mini-Me did on the Moon Base in the previous film before kicking the crap out of Austin. So, Austin not unreasonably thinks he's being suckered again and refuses to fall for this stunt twice (and thus doesn't realize it's not an act).

tropes.name: Totem Pole Trench
tropes.html: Invoked by Austin and Mini-Me during the infiltration of Dr. Evil's sub (albeit with Austin being the one on top).

tropes.name: Tough Room
tropes.html: Nobody laughs at Dr. Evil's "long and hard and full of seamen" joke, prompting him to say, "Tough sub."

tropes.name: Tractor Beam
tropes.html: Dr. Evil's plan this time around is to use a tractor beam to cause the Midas-22 asteroid to crash into Earth.

tropes.name: Twin Threesome Fantasy
tropes.html: Austin and the Japanese girls.

tropes.name: Ungrateful Bastard
tropes.html: Nigel shows little regard to Austin for saving him from an "unfortunate smelting accident", instead pointing out that Goldmember is getting away because of him.

tropes.name: Vocal Dissonance
tropes.html: Subverted in the Studio 69 scene, when Foxxy uses a man like a ventriloquist's dummy to speak to Austin covertly. At first glance, it seems like the guy is speaking with a sexy black woman's voice.

tropes.name: Wham Line
tropes.html:
Near the end when Nigel prevents Austin from shooting Dr. Evil:
Austin: Dr. Evil's not your son! I am!
Nigel: You both are.

tropes.name: What Happened to the Mouse?
tropes.html:
• Mr. Bigglesworth isn't seen at all, except in the flashback. But he appears in a deleted scene, where Dr. Evil remarks that holding him is like holding a hot ass.
  • Austin's Bond Girl from Shagged, Felicity Shagwell, is no where to be seen, nor is any explanation given for her absence. Looks like Basil was right when he said it wasn't meant to be.

tropes.name: Who's on First?
tropes.html: The Asian twins Fook Mi and Fook Yu. Austin is quite confused at first, but they evidently run into this problem on a regular basis and have their names on their bakcpacks.

tropes.name: Wire Fu
tropes.html: Parodied. Fat Bastard tries to use a Wire Fu attack on Austin (to the point of being visibly held up by wires and calling attention to the people in the background holding him up.) One of the wires breaks halfway through, though, and he's just left dangling in the air.

tropes.name: Yank the Dog's Chain
tropes.html:
Austin is bummed that his dad didn't attend his knighting ceremony. Later, Basil exposition informs Austin that his father was kidnapped:
Austin: Heavy, man. [perks up] OH! So that's why he wasn't at my knighting ceremony!
Basil: No, actually, he was kidnapped after you were knighted.
Austin: Ah.

tropes.name: Your Princess Is in Another Castle!
tropes.html: Austin gets Dr. Evil arrested in the very beginning, making it clear that something will inevitably go wrong. Dr. Evil even does a musical number pointing this out ("Austin caught me in the first act/it's all backwards, what's with that"?).
